newsitem.title: USA: Pa. court says no oral argument on tax case--paper.
newsitem.headline: Pa. court says no oral argument on tax case--paper.

text.p: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court said it would decide a case challenging the constitutionality of the personal property tax without hearing oral arguments, the Philadelphia Inquirer reported Tuesday.

The decision is a blow to Montgomery County, which was hoping to present expert testimony that the tax it wants the court to uphold is substantially different from one in North Carolina that the U.S. Supreme Court struck down in 1996, the newspaper said.

Billionaire Walter Annenberg is challenging the Pennsylvania tax, which is applied to the value of stocks of companies not registered to do business in Pennsylvania. The U.S. Supreme Court said North Carlina's tax unfairly penalized out-of-state companies.

Philadelphia is one of two municipalities in the state that continued collecting the tax even after it was challenged, and had asked the court to allow it to present arguments in support of Montgomery County's case. The court also turned down that request.
